item.title: Colour Impressions: Exploring Gelli Plate Monoprinting Workshop — Sun Oct 25, 3:00 PM — Aga Khan Museum
item.description:
Inspired by the Museum’s collections, this hands-on workshop explores the foundational elements of Islamic art, from geometry and proportion to rhythm and ornament, with a particular focus on geometric and floral motifs.
Through guided exploration and mindful experimentation with Gel plate monoprinting, participants will learn techniques such as layering, masking, and texture transfer to create original prints. This relaxed, process-oriented workshop invites reflection on the interplay between colour, form, and pattern, resulting in vibrant, one-of-a-kind works inspired by the timeless beauty of our collections.
Source: Aga Khan Museum

item.title: NEW EVENT - 👻🌙 The Ghosts of Cabbagetown — Tue Oct 27, 6:30 PM
item.description:
Try New Things in Toronto! # 👻🌙 The Ghosts of Cabbagetown
### A 90-Minute Evening Ghost Walk Through One of Toronto’s Most Historic Neighbourhoods
Cabbagetown has beautiful Victorian houses, quiet streets, old cemeteries, and a history that goes back generations. It also has ghosts.
Join me for a **90-minute evening walking tour through Cabbagetown**, where we'll explore some of the neighbourhood's strangest stories, unsettling legends, and darker pieces of Toronto's past.
We'll begin beneath the glass of **Allan Gardens**, then make our way through the streets of Cabbagetown, stopping along the way for stories of mysterious creatures, haunted buildings, old prisons, cemeteries, restless spirits, and the people who may never have quite left. This isn't a traditional history walk.
It's a **ghost tour** — so expect some history, some local legends, a little mystery, and a few stories that are difficult to explain. And, of course, we'll have a few laughs along the way.

item.title: 藍 ai - A life of creativity in Indigo by Sachiko Watanabe Opening Reception — Sat Jan 16, 2:00 PM — Japanese Canadian Cultural Centre
item.description: Artist Talk Sachiko Watanabe will share the story of ai (indigo), from growing plants to making dye material, demonstrating the traditional tools and techniques used to transform indigo plants into dye. Through her artwork and personal experiences, she will discuss the various indigo dyeing methods, her deep connection with nature, her lifestyle and the role that love and care play in her creative practice. The presentation will include: An introduction to the cultivation of indigo, the preparation of natural dye, and the artistic process behind her work. A video presentation showcasing her life, practice and creative journey. A Q&A session with the audience. Exhibition info Artist bio: Sachiko Watanabe (渡辺幸子) was born in 1977 in Ehime Prefecture, Japan. After studying textile design at Musashino Art University in Tokyo, she encountered natural indigo dye at the Iyo Kasuri Centre in Ehime.
